message.reasoning:
Let me assess the submission against the rubric.

C1: Mission concept and rationale (40% weight, levels 0-10 scaled). The student describes coral reef monitoring mission, GBR, users (marine and conservation scientists), rationale (bleaching events, 30% acidification, 2016/2017 bleaching losses), references (NOAA, NatGeo, deepreef, Nature). Good detail. However, mission requirements are not quantified (no orbit, resolution, revisit specified), and the "what it will do" is somewhat vague (near-real-time relay, SST, thermal stress, bathymetry). Still, clear and complete-ish description with literature references. I'd say Accomplished low end: 7-8. Let's say 7 or 8. The description is clear, relates function to users, references literature. Missing specific requirements/objectives quantified. I'd give 7.

C2: Project plan (30%). Gantt chart included with weeks, tasks, colour coding, deadlines. Task descriptions. Plan fits mission narrative somewhat (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL, STK). Contingencies? Not explicit — no provision for variations/contingencies. References to information sources included (useful links). The plan is robust but lacks explicit contingency. Adequate-to-Accomplished. The Gantt has some oddities: background research extends to week 8, STK simulations start week 4 before STK design (weeks 7-9) — slight inconsistency. Also "Strategies" week 3 only. Deadlines red lines. I'd say Accomplished low: 7. Hmm, contingency missing. The descriptor for Accomplished requires "provision for project variations and contingencies" and "makes clear why the plan is developed this way in the context of the mission." The student does explain rationale for each stage in context of mission. Contingency: week 10 reserved for review/amendments — arguably a buffer. I'd give 7.

C3: Preliminary progress (10%). Evidence: read Asner's system, researched bleaching, completed STK tutorials 1-4. That's minor work — no actual technical results (no orbit calcs, no link budget, no simulation results). "Minor work completed... Results description or interpretation may be insufficient." That's Adequate: 4-5. I'd give 4.

C4: Presentation (20%). Well-structured, headings, readable, references cited with superscripts and footnote URLs, useful links list. Figures: Gantt labelled with caption? The Gantt is an image with colour legend explained in text. References in text match reference list? The numbered footnotes 1-4 appear; the "Useful Links" list includes those plus more. Mostly consistent. Some issues: no figure caption/number for the Gantt (it's referenced as [Image 1] but in text "as seen above"). Formatting consistent. I'd say Accomplished low: 7-8. Writing is good. Give 8? The Gantt lacks a proper figure caption/number. Also the reference list is just URLs without titles. I'd give 7.

Requirements:
R1: met — mission concept, users, rationale.
R2: partial — plan relates to space segment (launch, orbit, ground control, comms, EOL) and mentions astrodynamics syllabus, but no actual application of course material/technical detail on launch and orbits yet. The plan includes those tasks. I'd say partial.
R3: met — STK selected, tutorials completed. Yes.
R4: met — Gantt chart.
R5: met — useful links.
R6: partial — only tutorials and reading; no technical results.

Technical issues:
- Gantt: STK Simulations (weeks 4-10) begins before STK Design (weeks 7-9) — sequencing inconsistency.
- Background research extends to week 8 while mission concept complete week 3 — minor.
- No quantified mission requirements (resolution, revisit, orbit).
- Claim "Oceans have become 30 percent more acidic" — actually 30% increase in acidity (pH decrease ~0.1), commonly stated as "30% more acidic" — acceptable but technically it's a 30% increase in hydrogen ion concentration. Minor.
- "bathymetry mapped to 100 m resolution" — fine.
- No software justification beyond STK tutorials.
- No contingency in plan.

Overall: solid preliminary report, strong concept, plan good, technical progress thin.

Marks: C1 7, C2 7, C3 4, C4 7.

Evidence quotes must be <=25 words, contiguous.

C1 evidence: "A near-real-time relay to monitoring stations on the ground would allow marine and conservation scientists to more accurately predict and react to coral bleaching events." That's 26 words? Count: A(1) near-real-time(2) relay(3) to(4) monitoring(5) stations(6) on(7) the(8) ground(9) would(10) allow(11) marine(12) and(13) conservation(14) scientists(15) to(16) more(17) accurately(18) predict(19) and(20) react(21) to(22) coral(23) bleaching(24) events(25). 25 words. OK.

C2 evidence: "Project work will be divided into weeks via a Gantt Chart. Detailed task descriptions can be found on the next page." 21 words. Good.

C3 evidence: "I have read the brief of Asner’s monitoring system in Hawaii, researched into how coral bleaching occurs and its severity, and also completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4." Count ~28 words. Too long. Use "completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4" — 7 words. Good.

C4 evidence: "Completed stages are gold. Incomplete stages are blue. Deadlines are indicated by red lines." 15 words.

Requirements where: section headings.

R2 where: "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress" — quote maybe "The syllabus work on astrodynamics will help me to understand and design an optimal mission." 16 words.

R3 where: "Project Plan & Preliminary Progress" quote "completed STK tutorials 1, 2, 3 & 4".

R6 where: same.

Technical issues with where.
